issues.description: Class constructor mismatch for GroverLightsOutPuzzle: the template implementation (template_repository/ex4_grover_lights_out_puzzle.py) declares def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) (requires an initial_state argument), while the solution implementation (solution_repository/ex4_grover_lights_out_puzzle.py) declares def __init__(self) (no argument). The template's own run/example usage (in the same template file) and the problem statement examples instantiate GroverLightsOutPuzzle() with no arguments. This inconsistency will raise a TypeError when students follow the provided run/example code and try to instantiate the class, and it creates ambiguity about whether the puzzle initial state should be supplied at construction time or when calling grover_circuit.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: remove the unused initial_state parameter from the template constructor (change def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) to def __init__(self):) so that instantiating GroverLightsOutPuzzle() (as shown in the run/example) works and the initial board is provided to grover_circuit via its state_of_lights argument. Alternatively, make the constructor parameter optional (def __init__(self, initial_state: Optional[list[int]] = None)) and update the run/example and grover_circuit usage to document the chosen behaviour.
